title: Short Stuff: The Devil's Den
summary: Short Stuff episode on the ghost stories of Devil's Den at the Gettysburg battlefield. The hosts open with Halloween-season banter, then give background on the 1863 Battle of Gettysburg (about 165,000 troops, roughly 7,000 dead over three days) and the fighting at Devil's Den between Big Round Top and Little Round Top, led by the Confederate First Texas under General John Bell Hood, including the Union artillery taken there and the Pickett's Charge the next day. They then recount alleged hauntings reported by visitors: a young soldier grabbing a climber's ankle, the "helpful hippie" barefoot Confederate figure who pointed the way, a second Texas-linked sighting, and cameras and phones malfunctioning in the area. Former park ranger and paranormal investigator Mark Nesbit (author of the Ghosts of Gettysburg series) is cited, including his theory that a staged photo of a dead sharpshooter caused the camera problems. The episode closes by noting the American Battlefield Trust's statement that orbs in photos are lens artifacts such as water or sunlight, not ghosts.

segments.title: Halloween banter and Gettysburg setup
segments.summary: Hosts open with Halloween-season chat and introduce the topic of Confederate and soldier ghosts at Gettysburg, noting the battle's heavy casualties.

segments.title: Devil's Den terrain and the Battle of Gettysburg
segments.summary: Describes the Battle of Gettysburg's scale and casualties, and the boulder-filled Devil's Den between Big and Little Round Top, which made fighting difficult and was the site of the Slaughter Pen.

segments.title: First Texas attack at Devil's Den and Pickett's Charge
segments.summary: Explains that the Confederate First Texas under John Bell Hood took Devil's Den on day two, capturing Union artillery, and that Pickett's Charge followed the next day and failed, giving the Union overall victory.

segments.title: Ghostly sightings at Devil's Den
segments.summary: Recounts visitor reports, including a soldier grabbing a climber's ankle and the barefoot 'helpful hippie' Confederate figure who pointed the way and vanished.

segments.title: Camera and phone problems and the staged photo theory
segments.summary: Visitors report phones and cameras failing at Devil's Den. Mark Nesbit suggests a staged photo of a dead sharpshooter, moved by the photographer, is behind the problems.

segments.title: Skeptical take on ghost orbs
segments.summary: The American Battlefield Trust says orbs in photos are water on the lens or sunlight, not ghosts. The hosts close by promoting further reading.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts sign off the Short Stuff episode.
